# MASTER'S RESEARCH — LIVER VIABILITY & ICG-NIR {#masters-research}

My Master's thesis investigates whether a stable ex vivo liver perfusion platform combined with
ICG-NIR fluorescence kinetics can provide quantitative indicators of liver function and viability.

### Need and hypothesis

**Need:** obtain a continuous, functional and non-destructive measurement of liver viability during ex vivo perfusion.

**Hypothesis:** ICG uptake and hepatobiliary excretion kinetics measured with NIR fluorescence contain parameters
that can help describe liver functional state.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    N["Need"] --> H["Hypothesis"]
    H --> O1["Objective 1<br/>Stable perfusion platform"]
    O1 --> O2["Objective 2<br/>Baseline without ICG"]
    O2 --> O3["Objective 3<br/>ICG-NIR functional marker"]
```

## Objective 1 — Ex Vivo Perfusion Platform {#objective-1}

Build and validate a stable and reproducible experimental platform capable of maintaining rat livers
under controlled physiological conditions.

### Perfusion circuit

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Reservoir"] --> B["Peristaltic Pump"]
    B --> C["Pulse Damper"]
    C --> D["Flow Sensor"]
    D --> E["Oxygenator"]
    E --> F["Bubble Trap"]
    F --> G["Liver"]
    G --> H["Return"]
```

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    FOTO DE LA PLATAFORMA DE PERFUSIÓN COMPLETA
    <small>Vista limpia del sistema armado y conectado</small>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    DIAGRAMA REAL DEL CIRCUITO DE PERFUSIÓN
    <small>Dirección de flujo, diámetros de tubería, sensores y componentes principales</small>
  </div>
</div>

### Pumping, pulse damping and oxygenation

The reservoir and peristaltic pump establish the perfusate flow. Because peristaltic pumping generates
pressure pulsations, a pulse-damping stage is used before the perfusate reaches the organ. Oxygenation
and bubble-removal stages support controlled perfusate conditions and reduce the risk of air entering the liver.

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    FOTO DEL DAMPER DE PULSACIONES
    <small>Componente utilizado para reducir los pulsos de presión de la bomba peristáltica</small>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    GRÁFICO ANTES Y DESPUÉS DEL DAMPER
    <small>Comparación de pulsaciones de presión o flujo</small>
  </div>
</div>

### Monitoring

The platform monitors:

- **P(t):** portal / pre-liver pressure.
- **Q(t):** portal perfusion flow.
- **T(t):** perfusate / organ temperature.
- **R(t)=P/Q:** vascular resistance.
- **pH / gases:** perfusate chemistry according to protocol.

<div class="image-slot large">
  <div class="slot-label">
    CAPTURA DEL MONITOR HIDRODINÁMICO
    <small>Presión, flujo, temperatura y resistencia vascular en tiempo real</small>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    FOTO DE SENSORES Y ELECTRÓNICA DE ADQUISICIÓN
    <small>Presión, flujo, temperatura, microcontrolador y conexiones</small>
  </div>
</div>

### Calibration and validation

Measurements are compared with reference instrumentation and characterized with quantitative metrics
such as correlation, deviation and RMSE.

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    FOTO DEL SETUP DE CALIBRACIÓN
    <small>Sistema desarrollado conectado al patrón de referencia</small>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    GRÁFICO DE CALIBRACIÓN / ERROR
    <small>Valor medido vs referencia, correlación, RMSE o desviación</small>
  </div>
</div>

**Objective 1 success criterion:** a reproducible experimental window in which the liver remains perfused,
thermally stable and its hemodynamic variables are continuously monitored.

## Objective 2 — Baseline Dataset without ICG {#objective-2}

Characterize the stability of the preparation and construct a physiological reference dataset before adding ICG.
This baseline is used to separate expected platform/preparation behavior from later fluorophore-related or
functional changes.

### Recorded variables

- Q(t) — portal flow.
- P(t) — portal pressure.
- T(t) — temperature.
- R(t)=P/Q — vascular resistance.
- pH / gases — perfusate state.

<div class="image-slot large">
  <div class="slot-label">
    FOTO DE UN EXPERIMENTO BASAL SIN ICG
    <small>Hígado perfundido durante una corrida utilizada para construir la línea base</small>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="image-slot large">
  <div class="slot-label">
    GRÁFICO BASAL DE PRESIÓN, FLUJO Y TEMPERATURA
    <small>Curvas alineadas temporalmente durante un experimento estable</small>
  </div>
</div>

### Vascular resistance and reproducibility

Vascular resistance provides a derived hemodynamic parameter for interpreting the pressure-flow relationship.
Repeated baseline experiments are used to estimate expected variability and verify that the platform provides
a sufficiently reproducible window.

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    GRÁFICO DE RESISTENCIA VASCULAR R(t)=P/Q
    <small>Evolución temporal y rango estable</small>

</div>

  </div>
</div>

## Objective 3 — ICG-NIR Functional Marker {#objective-3}

Develop a quantitative functional marker of liver viability from the temporal kinetics of ICG fluorescence.

### ICG experiment

ICG is introduced into perfusate containing albumin. Liver uptake and excretion are observed using
near-infrared fluorescence acquisition.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["ICG + albumin"] --> B["Liver uptake"]
    B --> C["NIR fluorescence"]
    C --> D["FI(t)"]
    D --> E["Kinetic parameters"]
```

<div class="image-slot large">
  <div class="slot-label">
    FOTO DEL MONTAJE EXPERIMENTAL ICG-NIR
    <small>Hígado, fuente NIR, filtros y sistema de adquisición</small>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    DIAGRAMA ÓPTICO DEL SISTEMA ICG-NIR
    <small>Excitación → hígado → emisión → filtro → adquisición</small>
  </div>
</div>

### Optical calibration and fluorescence kinetics

Before physiological interpretation, the system should characterize the relation between ICG concentration
and measured fluorescence under controlled conditions. The target signal is the temporal fluorescence curve,
FI(t), or a calibrated estimate of C_ICG(t).

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    CURVA CONCENTRACIÓN DE ICG VS FLUORESCENCIA
    <small>Rango lineal, saturación y región útil</small>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="image-slot large">
  <div class="slot-label">
    CURVA REPRESENTATIVA FI(t) DE ICG
    <small>Captación, peak y eliminación</small>
  </div>
</div>

### Functional parameters

Parameters to derive from the curve include:

- ICG-PDR — disappearance rate.
- ICG-R15 — retention at 15 minutes.
- ICG-CLR — clearance.
- Fmax.
- Tmax.
- Uptake / washout slopes.
- AUC.

<div class="image-slot">
  <div class="slot-label">
    CURVA ICG CON PDR, R15, CLEARANCE, FMAX, TMAX Y AUC
    <small>Parámetros cuantitativos extraídos desde FI(t)</small>
  </div>
</div>

### Experimental workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    S1["1<br/>Validate platform"] -->
    S2["2<br/>Baseline dataset"] -->
    S3["3<br/>ICG calibration"] -->
    S4["4<br/>Liver experiment"] -->
    S5["5<br/>Extract parameters"] -->
    S6["6<br/>Validate functional marker"]
```

The project integrates organ perfusion, fluidics, biomedical instrumentation, embedded systems,
signal acquisition, signal processing, biomedical optics, NIR fluorescence and experimental validation.

## CandelStim — Transcranial Electrical Stimulation {#candelstim}

Professional internship at Candel Medical Company focused on hardware, electronics and firmware for a
transcranial electrical stimulation medical device, improving an existing prototype toward a more integrated system.

### Stimulation modalities

- tDCS — transcranial direct current stimulation.
- tACS — transcranial alternating current stimulation.
- tRNS — transcranial random noise stimulation.

### Technical work

- Circuit analysis and redesign.
- Electronic component selection and simulation.
- PCB design, correction and debugging.
- ESP32 and STM32 development.
- Firmware modification and implementation.
- BLE communication.
- Signal generation and synchronization.
- Hardware/software integration.
- Energy-consumption reduction.
- Experimental validation and iterative troubleshooting.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    U["User / protocol"] --> F["Firmware"]
    F --> MCU["Microcontroller"]
    MCU --> E["Electronic circuitry"]
    E --> C["Current source"]
    C --> EL["Electrodes"]
```
